purpose: Maps Google Forms question titles to stable item ids, and maps the blind exercise cells to (asset_id, code). Written before any response was accessed. The Forms export uses question titles as column headers; this file is the only place those strings appear, so a title edit is a one-line fix here.

screening.years: Years working with digital assets professionally
screening.familiarity: How familiar are you with protocol-level mechanics such as fee burns, staking design and issuance schedules?
screening.allocator: Do you make or advise on allocation decisions in digital assets?

importance_grid.title: How much SHOULD each economic function matter to what a token is worth?

boundary_items.title: Does the token capture value from that revenue?
boundary_items.project_rule: No, this is a governance right only
options: No, this is a governance right only

boundary_items.title: Does the token capture value from usage?
For a classification made today, is the mechanism active?
Is the native token required in order to transact?
Is that value accruing to the token, or payment for a service?
Is that economically equivalent to destroying them?

materiality_items.title: At what point would you say an asset is materially used as collateral?
options: Above 1% of its own market cap
Above 5% of its own market cap
Both a dollar floor and a percentage floor

materiality_items.title: How long must a mechanism be live before you would count it in a classification?
options: No minimum, count it from activation

materiality_items.title: Should these functions be recorded as yes or no, or on a scale?
If evidence for a function is unavailable or ambiguous, what should the classification record?
options: Record it as unknown and exclude the asset from tests using it
Record a best estimate with a confidence flag

condition_dependent_note: An option is condition-dependent when adopting it would not yield a binary rule. 'Partially active' is condition-dependent for the same reason 'Depends' is: neither tells the codebook what to record.
duplicate_header_rule: Six scenario items are each followed by an identically titled 'Why? One line.' free-text item, so the Forms export contains six columns with the same header. The ingestion reads by column INDEX, not by name, and binds each free-text column to the scenario item immediately preceding it. csv.DictReader collapses duplicate headers and must not be used.

checkbox_items.title: What evidence would convince you a cryptoasset is genuinely used as money rather than merely traded?
options: Merchant or payment acceptance at scale
On-chain transfer value large relative to market cap
Held as a reserve asset by institutions or treasuries
Used as a unit of account for pricing
Material remittance or cross-border corridor volume
None of these are sufficient on their own

checkbox_items.title: What would make you trust a classification produced by researchers rather than a data vendor?
options: Primary sources cited for every decision
A second independent reviewer and a published agreement statistic
Open code that regenerates every number
Nothing would, I would use a vendor

checkbox_analysis_rule: Checkbox items are multi-select. They are reported as selection rate per option over respondents who answered the item, never as a consensus level, because the options are not mutually exclusive and no plurality rule applies. Co-selection counts for the pairs that matter are reported alongside. Splitting on the comma separator is ambiguous when an 'Other' answer contains a comma, so any answer that does not parse cleanly into listed options is carried verbatim and counted under an explicit unparsed category rather than silently dropped.

single_choice_items.title: Should technical architecture be treated as part of a token’s economic profile, or kept separate as context?
Which would be most useful in your work?
options: A model estimating fair value from a token’s functions
A model estimating risk profile — market sensitivity, drawdown, volatility — from its functions
The classification itself, applied by me
A screening tool that flags mismatches between price and function

free_text_items.title: Is anything missing from that list of ten, or is anything on it redundant?
Suppose a classification told you an asset is monetary, collateral-eligible and supply-capped, with no revenue capture. What, if anything, would you do differently?
Anything you would want this research to answer that it currently does not?
Any cell where the rule felt wrong, ambiguous, or impossible to apply? Tell us which and why.

free_text_rule: Grouping free text by argument is a human coding step and is not automated. The module emits every free-text answer verbatim into a coding worksheet with a stable response id and an empty argument_group column, and reports response counts and coverage only. No free-text summary statistic is produced by code.

frozen_prediction.statement: Revenue capture and monetary use rank in the top three; incentives and governance rank in the bottom three.
